The chef prepared a delicious dish.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Money won in gambling or lottery. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'игрыш'). Common masculine noun meaning 'winnings, prize, win' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Вот это да, забери свой большой выигрыш!
examples.trans: Wow look at that, take your big winnings!

examples.text: Пожалуйста, вот ваш выигрыш, забирайте фишки.
examples.trans: Please, here is your winnings, take the chips.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('stupid, silly, foolish').

examples.text: Ваня, ты глупый? Зачем ты сейчас это при нём сказал?
examples.trans: Vanya, are you stupid? Why did you just say that in front of him?

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Я тебе говорю = I'm telling you. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.

meanings.en: hot (to the touch, of food/drink, not weather)
meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('hot').

examples.trans: Careful, the cup is very hot.

examples.text: Аркаша, держи горячий чай. И бутерброд с вареньем ешь.
examples.trans: Arkasha, here's some hot tea. And eat a jam sandwich.

meanings.note: В гости = for a visit. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guest, visitor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, к вам гости! Па-пам!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, you have visitors! Ta-da!

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to prepare, get ready', paired with 'приготовиться'.

examples.trans: We are simply preparing for the morning show.
The students were preparing for the exam.
And little Grisha is preparing for the morning show.

meanings.note: usually the short form: я готов (m), я готова (f)
plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: The money is on the table.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'team; command' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'team; command' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ничего страшного. Теперь мы одна команда.
examples.trans: Nothing serious. Now we're one team.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'feed, food (for animals)' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Настя купила в магазине специальный корм для бездомных котят.
examples.trans: Nastya bought special food for stray kittens at the store.

examples.text: Для рыб в ресторанном аквариуме нужен дорогой сухой корм.
examples.trans: Expensive dry food is needed for the fish in the restaurant aquarium.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to buy', paired with 'покупать'.

examples.text: Юле бы дублёнку купили, Славику бы ноутбук.
examples.trans: We could have bought Yulia a sheepskin coat, and Slavik a laptop.

meanings.note: в кухне / на кухне = in the kitchen, на кухню = to the kitchen
E.g. русская кухня. Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.trans: And the kitchen is over there.
We are sitting in the kitchen.

examples.text: Проходите, пожалуйста! Как видите, большой коридор, а там кухня.
examples.trans: Come on in, please! As you can see, a big hall, and the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Аникеев лично сюда приезжал, и что?
examples.trans: Anikeev came here in person, and what?

examples.text: Пятнадцать лет мы просим новое здание! Аникеев лично сюда приезжал, и что?
examples.trans: For fifteen years we've been asking for a new building! Anikeev came here in person, and what?

meanings.note: В любой момент = at any moment. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('any').

examples.text: Любая обезьяна эти выборы выиграет! Ты что, хуже обезьяны?
examples.trans: Any monkey will win this election! What, are you worse than a monkey?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'minute' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: All right, stay there. I'll be there in ten minutes.

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.

Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'довольный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('dissatisfied, unhappy').

examples.text: Славик, ну ты вечно всем недоволен!
examples.trans: Slavik, you are always dissatisfied with everything!

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ычный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('ordinary, usual').

examples.text: Да нет на него никакого компромата. Обычный мужик.
examples.trans: There is no compromising material on him at all. Just an ordinary guy.

examples.text: Я просто пошла на обычный концерт.
examples.trans: I simply went to an ordinary concert.

meanings.note: From German 'Offiziant' / Late Latin 'officians' (one who performs a duty or service).

examples.trans: The waiter politely greets the new guests.
Please do not block the walkway for the waiters.

meanings.note: Irregular plural повара. Common masculine noun meaning 'cook, chef' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

meanings.note: Подожди! = wait!. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait (a while)', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: On foot. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go (set off)', paired with 'идти'.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'stream, flow, rush' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Официанты не справляются с таким потоком.
examples.trans: The waiters cannot cope with such a flow.

examples.text: Там такие деньги! Деньги рекой потекут.
examples.trans: There's so much money in it! Money will flow like a river.

meanings.note: Asks about the reason. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чему').

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine
as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нцип'). Common masculine noun meaning 'principle' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Сейчас деньги важнее любых глупых принципов.
examples.trans: Now money is more important than any silly principles.

examples.text: В принципе, вкус нормальный и не плохой.
examples.trans: In principle, the taste is fine and not bad.

meanings.en: to happen, take place, go on
meanings.note: Что происходит? = What is going on?

examples.trans: What is going on? I don't understand.

examples.text: Мы не знаем, что с нашей дочерью происходит!
examples.trans: We don't know what is happening with our daughter!

meanings.note: Прямо так = just like that. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: В смысле, Виктор Степанович? Прямо так, да?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?

meanings.note: + 3rd person verb: 'пусть строят' = let them build

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: + genitive plural: пять рублей. Core Russian num meaning 'five' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы же только начинаем. Через месяц будет пять тысяч.
examples.trans: But we're only just starting. In a month there'll be five thousand.

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Рабочее место = job, workplace. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('working; work').
As a noun. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('working; work').

examples.trans: We will build the cluster. That means thousands of jobs.

meanings.note: Dining establishment. Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

examples.text: Ты отлично справляешься сегодня на смене.
examples.trans: You are doing great on the shift today.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тейк'). Common masculine noun meaning 'steak' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: At the start of a question. Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.
Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.
